Since all of our questions required different information and formatting, I ended up making a dataset for each question.
We will want to use seasonal_monthly for our second research question. We could also use it for the first question but birds_monthy and birds_monthly_fam is probably preferable for that application. The season_strain data set should be used for the third research question. At this point, based on our outline I havve only included the families in birds_monthly_fam if we have enough data/power for our analysis and it is found significant in the first question, I can pull it in for the others but for now I wanted to avoid too many bins

Family labels done by Allison

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Mammal families
hpai_mammals <- mammals_orig %>%
  mutate(captive = str_detect(Species, "\\(captive\\)"),
         species_clean = Species %>% str_remove("\\s*\\(captive\\)") %>%
           str_squish() %>% str_to_lower())

hpai_mammals <- hpai_mammals %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      species_clean == "domestic cat" ~ "Domestic cat",
      species_clean %in% c("bobcat", "mountain lion", "canada lynx", "eurasian lynx",
                           "african lion", "amur leopard", "tiger", "amur tiger",
                           "bengal tiger", "hybrid tiger", "geoffroy's cat", "serval",
                           "savannah cat") ~ "Non-domestic felid",
      species_clean %in% c("red fox", "gray fox", "arctic fox", "catalina island fox",
                           "fox (unidentified)", "coyote") ~ "Canid",
      species_clean %in% c("american black bear", "black bear", "grizzly bear",
                           "kodiak bear", "polar bear") ~ "Bear",
      species_clean %in% c("american mink", "american marten", "fisher", "ermine",
                           "long-tailed weasel", "north american river otter") ~ "Mustelid",
      species_clean %in% c("raccoon", "striped skunk", "skunk (unidentified)") ~ "Raccoon & skunk",
      species_clean %in% c("bottlenose dolphin", "california sea lion", "grey seal",
                           "harbor seal", "northern elephant seal", "sea otter") ~ "Marine mammal",
      species_clean %in% c("house mouse", "deer mouse", "black rat", "norway rat",
                           "prairie vole", "muskrat", "abert's squirrel",
                           "eastern gray squirrel", "round-tailed ground squirrel",
                           "thirteen-lined ground squirrel") ~ "Rodent",
      species_clean == "desert cottontail" ~ "Lagomorph",
      species_clean == "virginia opossum" ~ "Opossum",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    family = case_when(
      group %in% c("Domestic cat", "Non-domestic felid") ~ "Felidae",
      group == "Canid" ~ "Canidae",
      group == "Bear" ~ "Ursidae",
      species_clean == "raccoon" ~ "Procyonidae",
      species_clean %in% c("striped skunk", "skunk (unidentified)") ~ "Mephitidae",
      species_clean %in% c("bottlenose dolphin") ~ "Delphinidae",
      species_clean == "california sea lion" ~ "Otariidae",
      species_clean %in% c("grey seal", "harbor seal", "northern elephant seal") ~ "Phocidae",
      group == "Mustelid" | species_clean == "sea otter" ~ "Mustelidae",
      species_clean %in% c("house mouse", "black rat", "norway rat") ~ "Muridae",
      species_clean %in% c("deer mouse", "prairie vole", "muskrat") ~ "Cricetidae",
      str_detect(species_clean, "squirrel") ~ "Sciuridae",
      group == "Lagomorph" ~ "Leporidae",
      group == "Opossum" ~ "Didelphidae",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

table(hpai_mammals$family)
```

Different date ranges

```{r}
range(hpai_mammals$Date.Collected, na.rm = TRUE)
range(hpai_birds$Collection.Date, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Convert dates to date objects, fill missing values in the Collection.Date with the Date.Detected. Filter to only the bird species with at least 500 cases over time and filter both data sets to be the same time frame with only complete months. Also removed observations for which the county was unknown.

```{r}
library(lubridate)

hpai_mammals$Date.Collected <- as.Date(hpai_mammals$Date.Collected, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
hpai_mammals$Date.Detected <- as.Date(hpai_mammals$Date.Detected, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

hpai_birds <- hpai_birds %>%
  mutate(Collection.Date = na_if(Collection.Date, "Unknown"),
    Collection.Date = coalesce(Collection.Date, Date.Detected),
    Collection.Date = as.Date(Collection.Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    Date.Detected = as.Date(Date.Detected, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))

hpai_birds <- hpai_birds %>% filter(Collection.Date >= as.Date("2022-04-01") & Collection.Date <= as.Date("2026-08-31")) %>% filter(County != "Unknown")

species500 <- hpai_birds %>%
  filter(WOAH.Classification == "Wild bird") %>%
  count(family) %>%
  filter(n > 500) %>%
  pull(family)

birds <- hpai_birds %>% filter(family %in% species500) 
mammals <- hpai_mammals %>% filter(Date.Collected <= as.Date("2026-08-31") & Date.Collected >= as.Date("2022-04-01"))
```

```{r}
dim(birds)
dim(mammals)
```


Aggregating cases by county and month

```{r}
mammal_monthly <- mammals %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(Date.Collected, "month")) %>%
  count(State, County, year_month, name = "m_cases")
#mammal_monthly

bird_monthly <- birds %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(Collection.Date, "month")) %>%
  count(State, County, year_month, name = "b_cases")
#bird_monthly

bird_monthly_fam <- birds %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(Collection.Date, "month")) %>%
  count(State, County, year_month, family, name = "case_per_family") %>%
  mutate(total_county_cases = sum(case_per_family), .by = c(State, County, year_month))
#bird_monthly_fam

monthly_cases <-bird_monthly %>%
  full_join(mammal_monthly, by = c("State", "County", "year_month")) %>%
  mutate(b_cases = coalesce(b_cases, 0), m_cases = coalesce(m_cases, 0),
    total_cases = b_cases + m_cases)

#head(monthly_cases)
```

There don't appear to be enough mammal cases for the monthly breakdown to work well. The seasonal aggregates work better but still may struggle to be informative

Can easily change the names or timing of the seasons to be more backed by existing bird migration expertise, if appropriate. 

```{r}
seasonal_cases <- monthly_cases %>%
  mutate(Year = year(ymd(year_month)),
    month_num = month(ymd(year_month)),
    Season = case_when(month_num %in% 3:5  ~ "Spring",
      month_num %in% 6:8  ~ "Summer",
      month_num %in% 9:11 ~ "Fall",
      TRUE                ~ "Winter" )) %>%
  group_by(State, County, Year, Season) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = sum(total_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    b_cases = sum(b_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    m_cases = sum(m_cases, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

head(seasonal_cases)
```

Reaggregate by strain for the third research question

```{r}
m_month_strain <- mammals %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(Date.Collected, "month")) %>%
  count(State, County, year_month, HPAI.Strain, name = "m_cases")

b_month_strain <- birds %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(Collection.Date, "month")) %>%
  count(State, County, year_month, HPAI.Strain, name = "b_cases")

month_strain <- b_month_strain %>% 
  full_join(m_month_strain, by = c("State", "County", "year_month", "HPAI.Strain")) %>%
  mutate(b_cases = coalesce(b_cases, 0), m_cases = coalesce(m_cases, 0), total_cases = b_cases + m_cases)

season_strain <- month_strain %>%
  mutate(Year = year(year_month),
    month_num = month(year_month),
    Season = case_when(month_num %in% 3:5  ~ "Spring",
      month_num %in% 6:8  ~ "Summer",
      month_num %in% 9:11 ~ "Fall",
      TRUE                ~ "Winter")) %>%
  group_by(State, County, Year, Season, HPAI.Strain) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = sum(total_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    b_cases = sum(b_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    m_cases = sum(m_cases, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

head(season_strain)
```

We will want to use seasonal_monthly for our second research question. We could also use it for the first question but birds_monthy and birds_monthly_fam is probably preferable for that application. The season_strain data set should be used for the third research question.

## Basic Plot

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tigris)
library(sf)
library(viridis)

county_shapes <- tigris::counties(cb = TRUE, year = 2020) 

states_dc <- c(state.name, "District of Columbia")
county_shapes <- county_shapes %>% filter(STATE_NAME %in% states_dc)
county_shapes <- tigris::shift_geometry(county_shapes) # Need this so plots are centered and not too small

# Can repeat similar process to get plots by season or family
cases_annual <- seasonal_cases %>%
  group_by(State, County, Year) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = sum(total_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    b_cases = sum(b_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    m_cases = sum(m_cases, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

Examine the cases that didn't match original boundaries. Seven counties that made up almost two thousand observations.

```{r}
unmatched_cases <- cases_annual %>% distinct(State, County) %>%
  anti_join(county_shapes %>%  st_drop_geometry() %>% distinct(STATE_NAME, NAME),
    by = c("State" = "STATE_NAME", "County" = "NAME"))

unmatched_cases
```

Can resolve the mismatch manually from how the data was recorded with a simple change in capitalization or punctuation in all but one case. One county in Alaska was split into multiple counties in 2017, since this is only one observation and we have no way of knowing which modern county it would fall into, we have chosen to omit this one point from our analysis.

```{r}
cases_map_clean <- seasonal_cases %>%
  mutate(State = recode(State, "DC" = "District of Columbia"),
    County = recode(County,
      "Mcintosh" = "McIntosh",
      "St Clair" = "St. Clair",
      "Noble" = "Nobles",
      "St Lawrence" = "St. Lawrence",
      "St Croix" = "St. Croix"))
```


```{r}
years <- sort(unique(cases_annual$Year))

map_data <- purrr::map_dfr(years, function(y) {
  county_shapes %>%
    mutate(Year = y) %>%
    left_join(cases_annual %>%
        filter(Year == y) %>%
        select(-Year), by = c("NAME" = "County", "STATE_NAME" = "State"))})
```


```{r}
ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = total_cases), color = "white", linewidth = 0.08) +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", na.value = "grey85", name = "Total cases") +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Total HPAI Cases by County Annually") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```
